caseno: CIVIL PETITION FOR LEAVE TO APPEAL NO. 45 OF 1995
lawyer:
For the Petitioner: Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, Advocate, instructed by Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record. 
Respondents: Not Represented
parties:
Platinum Jubilee Jute Mills Ltd. ------ Petitioner
Versus
Chairman, Khulna Labour Court, Khulna Division, Khulna and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 5. Mr. Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner firstly, contended that the High Court Division failed to consider that respondent No. 3 who controls the activities of the petitioner's Jute Mills having been impleaded as a party in the complaint case while the petitioner Jute Mills is located at Khalishpur, Khulna the case fell within the concurrent jurisdiction of Khulna Labour Court and Dhaka Labour Court and as such the proper forum for the case was the Second Labour Court at Dhaka, The learned Advocate raised the same point before the High Court Division and in support of his contention referred to the case of Md. Mahmudul Haque V. Md. Shamsul Alam reported in 36 DLR (AD) 179. The learned Judges of the High Court Division rightly held that the cited case was not applicable to the instant case in as much as the petitioner Mills is located at Khalishpur, Khulna. Further this question of jurisdiction was not raised by the petitioner before the Labour Court. The learned Advocate has secondly contended that the Labour Court has committed an error of law in entering into the merit of the Enquiry Report and wrongly held that no offence of theft was committed by respondent No. 2, although the Labour Court found no procedural defect in holding the Departmental enquiry. But in the instant case the question was whether the charge framed against respondent No. 2 constituted an offence of theft. Admittedly there was no removal of` any goods from the possession of the petitioner Mills by respondent No. 2 and as such the Labour Court rightly found that there was no offence of theft. At the most the delinquent might have been charged for an attempt to realise enhanced wages by showing increased number of work; but the delinquent was charged for committing the offence of theft. As such the charge framed against the delinquent was a misconceived one and it cannot be said that the Labour Court sat on a judgment over the findings of the domestic enquiry committee.
